title: LingBot-Video: A Sparse-MoE Video Diffusion World Model
hook: Video diffusion models are usually dense — every parameter fires on every frame. LingBot-Video swaps in a sparse Mixture-of-Experts, then grades its own physics with a VLM judge.
key_points: Single-stream diffusion transformer using a DeepSeek-V3-style sparse MoE: 128 experts, top-8 routing, 1.4B active of 13B total parameters.
Post-trained with six-reward RL, including a physical-plausibility reward scored by a VLM judging sampled frames.
Also supports action-to-video mode: predicts robot rollout videos conditioned on action and hand-pose streams.
Open weights, code, and a Diffusers/SGLang inference stack released under the LingBot-Video name.
Raises its own Goodhart's-law question: can a VLM reliably judge physics, or will the reward just get gamed?
content_html: Most video diffusion models are dense — every parameter does work on every frame, whether or not that capacity is needed. LingBot-Video bets on sparsity instead, borrowing DeepSeek-V3's Mixture-of-Experts recipe for a video world model.
extra_html: The architecture is a single-stream diffusion transformer with 128 experts per MoE layer and top-8 routing, so only 1.4B of its 13B total parameters activate per forward pass — trading a bigger model for cheaper inference. Post-training layers in six reward signals, one of them scoring physical plausibility by having a vision-language model judge sampled frames. The team also released an action-to-video mode, conditioning generation on action and hand-pose streams to predict robot rollout videos, plus open weights, code, and a Diffusers/SGLang serving stack. Posted to r/MachineLearning, 2026-07-08, the release author raised their own flag on the physics reward: grading plausibility with a VLM is convenient, but it's exactly the kind of proxy metric Goodhart's law warns about — a model can learn to look physically right to the judge without the underlying dynamics actually improving.

related.title: LingBot-World 2.0: An Agent-Piloted Infinite World Model
related.hook: Interactive world models usually run out of road — quality degrades, or the action set stays thin. LingBot-World 2.0 stays coherent forever and puts an agent inside to invent what's next.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

related.title: Switch Transformer: Scaling to Trillion-Parameter Models
related.hook: Route every token to exactly one expert instead of many - this single simplification made trillion-parameter MoE models stable enough to train at scale.

related.title: LingBot-Vision: Boundary-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining
related.hook: Masked-patch pretraining hopes boundary structure emerges on its own. This method forces the issue, masking exactly the regions a student can't infer by copying context — and beats a 7B model at 1.1B.

flashcards.prompt: What's the core architectural bet behind LingBot-Video?
flashcards.back_html: It's a single-stream video diffusion transformer that swaps a dense feed-forward stack for a DeepSeek-V3-style sparse MoE — 128 experts, top-8 routing — so only 1.4B of its 13B total parameters activate per token.

flashcards.prompt: What concern does the release itself raise about LingBot-Video's physical-plausibility reward?

choices.text: A VLM grades physics from sampled frames, which may be gameable rather than a reliable judge of real physical plausibility
The reward is computed by running a physics simulator on every frame
There is no physical-plausibility reward in the training recipe
Physical plausibility is measured by human annotators only

flashcards.explanation_html: The release uses a VLM to judge physical plausibility from sampled frames — convenient, but the author flags Goodhart's law: a proxy judge can be gamed without the underlying physics actually improving.

flashcards.prompt: Besides ordinary text-to-video, what extra mode does LingBot-Video support?
flashcards.back_html: An action-to-video mode: given action and hand-pose conditioning, it predicts robot rollout videos, extending the same diffusion backbone toward embodied/robotics use.
